records.source_title: 02-19-2026 00:05:05 Legion pro 32UD-10 HDR modes byMetasotkuinY Gaming Accessories & Curved Gaming Monitors Hi What HDR modes give the full 1000 nit brightness?
records.author: Adriel_lenovo
records.text:
Hi and welcome to the Lenovo Community
Metasotku
,
I understand your question on if what HDR mode will give 1000 nit full brightness on the Lenovo Legion Pro 32UD-10 monitor.
To address your concern:
• Peak brightness: The advertised 1000‑nit level is reached only during HDR playback with appropriate scene content (small bright highlights) and with local dimming active. The specific HDR preset that consistently drives full peak luminance can vary by content and settings; please refer to the monitor’s PSREF/spec sheet for the official brightness spec and supported HDR formats: Lenovo Product Specifications Reference (PSREF) by clicking
here
.
• Oversaturated colors in HDR Photo/Movie/Gaming: Those presets are tuned for a more vivid look and can oversaturate compared to accurate HDR tone mapping. To reduce oversaturation: - In the monitor OSD, switch from the HDR “Photo/Movie/Gaming” presets to a more neutral/standard HDR mode if available, or select a user/custom mode and set Color Gamut to Auto or sRGB. - Disable any image enhancement features (e.g., dynamic contrast, vivid/color boost) within the OSD when using HDR. - Ensure the GPU output is set to full-range and high bit depth (e.g., RGB Full, 10‑bit where supported) in your graphics control panel. - Re‑enable local dimming for correct HDR contrast. - Calibrate HDR in the OS (Windows HDR settings and calibration) and confirm your content is HDR10.
• Firmware/updates: If the OSD does not provide a neutral HDR preset or you still see over‑saturation after the steps above, check for the latest monitor firmware/driver on the Lenovo Support site via this other
link
.
Hope this helps.
Thanks,
Adriel_Lenovo
